Commentary.Commentary: The umpires and the players have taken the field. Travis Head and David Warner are the openers for Australia. Lungi Ngidi to start the attack for South Africa. Lets play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...
Australia chasing 419 in 50 overs.

Australia, in contrast, struggled to find their rhythm, especially in the death overs. Their bowling, marred by numerous full tosses and short deliveries, allowed the South African batters to rack up boundaries with ease. While the batting conditions favored the Proteas, Australia's bowlers will undoubtedly see this game as a learning experience. Now, with the conditions still looking favorable for batters, Josh Hazlewood picked up a couple of wickets but also ended with his most expensive spell in ODIs while Adam Zampa had an off day. Marcus Stoinis, Nathan Ellis, and Michael Neser chipped in with one wicket each. Australia faces the uphill task of chasing down 419 runs in their 50 overs to secure the series. The stage is set for an exhilarating second innings, where either the Aussies will seize victory and the series or the Proteas will take it to the final game. Let's stay tuned to see how this thrilling encounter unfolds.

Heinrich Klaasen, the man of the moment is up for a quick chat. He says that it feels incredible. Adds that he and Rassie van der Dussen gave themselves a couple of extra as the wicket was a bit slow initially. Tells that once Rassie took on the bowling, they just continued the momentum. Mentions that this is definitely one of the best knocks for him and it is extra special as this is his home ground. Says that the wicket is good and they felt that after the 35th over they took control. Reckons that they should be able to defend this one.

South Africa's innings began cautiously, with the openers carefully gauging the conditions and defending their wickets. They stitched together a solid opening partnership of 64 runs, denying the Australian bowlers early breakthroughs. However, it was Rassie van der Dussen who truly set the stage with a masterful 62, laying the foundation for Heinrich Klaasen's mind-blowing 174 off just 83 balls. The explosive partnership between Klaasen and David Miller, who contributed with 82 off 45 balls, yielded more than 200 runs in under 15 overs, propelling South Africa to this colossal total.

A breathtaking innings from Heinrich Klaasen! David Miller's knock was equally important as well as the first innings of this pivotal game in the five-match ODI series between Australia and South Africa concluded with a jaw-dropping display of batting prowess from the Proteas. The hosts batting first, posted an astonishing total of 418 for the loss of just 5 wickets which is the highest ever on this ground in this format. A mountainous target now stands as a daunting challenge for the Aussies.

OUT! TAKEN! An anti-climatic end to the innings! Marcus Stoinis lands this short again and around leg, Heinrich Klaasen goes through his pull shot a bit early and mistimes it in the air wide of deep square leg where Nathan Ellis runs to his right and manages to hold on to it, tumbling on the ground. Klaasen walks out with a round of applause from everyone present on the ground. South Africa end on a massive 416/5!

Adds that they batted well in the last game and will look to do more of the same and hopes the wicket stays the same. Tells that it is a lot to balance with the World Coming up but they are up for the challenge. Informs Bavuma misses out and Rassie van der Dussen gets another chance while Kagiso Rabada and Lungi Ngidi are in as well. Ends by saying that anything around 300-320 would be a good score.

Mitchel Marsh, the skipper of Australia says that they will bowl first. Adds that it's a really good surface and they will look to pick up early wickets to put them under pressure from the start. He talks about his captaincy for Australia and winning a series and also about the upcoming World Cup as he mentions that the team has found a good combination and will hope the forms continue till the main stage. Informs Adam Zampa comes in while Michael Neser is also playing in this game. Ends by saying that they are focused on the intent for the results and hopefully go on to win the game.

Aiden Markram's exceptional century, a blazing 102 off just 74 balls featuring 9 boundaries and 4 towering sixes, was the standout performance. This match takes on a do-or-die significance for South Africa, a must-win if they hope to stay in the race for the series title. The Australia tour of South Africa has delivered some of the most memorable matches, and we are now at Centurion for the fourth ODI between these two teams. The visitors lead the series by 2-1 as of now. The Aussies will look to win this game and wrap up this series. They would be happy with their performance so far. However, with a loss in their last game, they will look to leave that behind and get back to winning ways. They were outplayed in their last encounter as they ended up with a mammoth total of 339 to chase and were bowled out for 227 runs. David Warner continued with his good form and was their top scorer with 78 runs. He along with Travis Head were the only two players to go past the 30-run mark in the last game. Marnus Labuschagne, who was in a pretty good touch for the last two games was also dismissed for a low score. The batting form of Tim David and Mitchell Marsh will be a topic of concern for them. The bowling unit also had a bad day as they leaked a lot of runs.  Josh Hazlewood looked out of his rhythm as he will hope to be in the wickets once again in this match. On the other hand, South Africa has been totally outplayed at home, but a victory in their previous game would have given them a big boost. They will be confident heading into this game and will aim to push the series into the decider. Aiden Markram was fantastic in the last game as he scored 102 along with Quinton de Kock also scored a brilliant 82. Marco Jansen played a brilliant cameo toward the end of the innings and provided a much-needed boost. The form of the rest of their batters will be a topic of discussion as they lack consistency. The bowling department had a really good total to defend, and they made sure the job was well done. Gerald Coetzee picked up a four-fer in the last game and he will look to continue with the same momentum. Tabraiz Shamsi and Keshav Maharaj weaved their spin magic and troubled the batters in the middle phases. So, will the Aussies win this game and seal the series? Or will the hosts keep the series alive with another win? Only time will tell.
